{{Short description|British policy council}}
The '''Advisory Committee on Mathematics Education''' ('''ACME''') is a British policy council for the [[Royal Society]] based in [[London, England]]. Founded in 2002 by the Royal Society and the [[Joint Mathematical Council]], ACME analyzes mathematics education practices and provides advice on education policy. ACME is funded by the [[Gatsby Charitable Foundation]] (2002–2015) and the [[Department for Education]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acme-uk.org|title=Advisory Committee on Mathematics Education - ACME|first=ACME - Advisory Committee on Mathematics|last=Education|website=www.acme-uk.org}}</ref>

==Members==
The committee chair is appointed for a three-year term. As of 2018, the membership<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/committees/advisory-committee-on-mathematics-education-acme/|title=Advisory Committee on Mathematics Education (ACME) - Royal Society|website=royalsociety.org}}</ref> is composed of:

* [[Frank Kelly (mathematician)|Frank Kelly]] (Chair)

*[[Paul Glaister]]
*Paul Golby
*Jeremy Hodgen
